title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models

children.title: Foundations, Surveys, and Taxonomies of RAG
Foundational RAG Proposal and Seminal Architecture
children.rationale: This paper introduces the original RAG framework as a differentiable retrieval-augmented model for knowledge-intensive NLP, serving as the conceptual anchor for all subsequent survey and taxonomy work.

children.title: Comprehensive Surveys and Broad Taxonomies of RAG for LLMs
children.rationale: These papers provide wide-scope reviews of RAG in the LLM era, covering overall paradigms, evolution, architecture components, limitations (hallucination, staleness), and general taxonomies across retrieval and generation stages.

children.title: Specialized Taxonomies and Extended Perspectives on RAG
children.rationale: These works extend or refine RAG taxonomies along specific axes—retrieval fusion techniques, knowledge-oriented retrieval, retrieval-augmented understanding (RAU) alongside RAG, and workshop-driven identification of open problems—offering more targeted or alternative classificatory lenses.
These papers establish the RAG paradigm, provide comprehensive surveys, and define taxonomies that frame the entire field.

children.title: Core RAG Methods: Retrieval, Fusion, and Generation Techniques
Query Formulation and Document Retrieval Strategies
Document Retrieval Mechanisms: Dense Retrieval, Relevance, and Diversity
children.rationale: These papers address how documents are retrieved and ranked—enhancing DPR with control tokens, ensuring diversity via information gain, and dynamically expanding retrieval through multi-hop document relevance—focusing on the retrieval model and scoring side of the pipeline.

children.title: Query Formulation and Optimization Strategies for RAG
children.rationale: These papers focus on how queries are constructed, refined, or blended—using LLM-based query generation with alignment scoring and combining internal/external knowledge augmentation—to improve the quality of the query signal sent to the retriever.

These papers all focus on the upstream retrieval stage: how queries are constructed, refined, or optimized, and how documents are selected or re-ranked to improve recall and precision before any generation occurs.

children.title: Retrieval–Generation Fusion: Bridging the Semantic Gap and Iterative Synergy
Bridging the Semantic Gap: Architectural and Structural Alignment Between Retrievers and Generators
children.rationale: These papers diagnose and remedy the structural mismatch between retrieval and generation components—R²AG injects retrieval signals into the LLM, KG²RAG uses knowledge graphs to supply relational context, and context-guided dynamic retrieval builds differentiable joint-training pathways—all targeting the static alignment problem.

children.title: Iterative and Unified Retrieval-Generation Synergy: Dynamic Coupling and Query-Free Integration
children.rationale: These papers move beyond one-shot retrieval by having generation actively drive retrieval across multiple rounds (iterative synergy) or by collapsing the retrieval-generation boundary entirely into a single model with implicit queries (ImpRAG), representing the frontier of tight retrieval-generation coupling.

These papers address the interface between retrieval and generation—how retrieval signals, knowledge-graph structure, or implicit queries are incorporated into the generation process, and how iterative or dynamic feedback loops tighten the coupling between the two modules.

children.title: End-to-End Training, Unified Architectures, and Generation-Side Optimization
children.rationale: These papers move beyond pipeline-level fixes to propose jointly trained or unified models—generative retrieval, direct retrieval-augmented optimization, hierarchical instruction tuning, and interpretability tooling—that optimize the full RAG system at the generation or system level.
These papers propose or analyze specific technical mechanisms for improving retrieval quality, query formulation, document relevance, and retrieval-generation integration.

children.title: Evaluation, Benchmarking, and Comparative Analysis of RAG Systems
Survey and Frameworks for RAG Evaluation Methodology
children.rationale: These papers take a meta-level view, surveying evaluation processes, metrics, and frameworks across RAG systems rather than running a single focused experiment.

children.title: Empirical Benchmarking and Comparative Experiments on RAG Systems
children.rationale: These papers conduct hands-on empirical evaluations—comparing retrieval vs. generation approaches on ODQA, probing LLM-specific RAG abilities, and introducing modular multi-modal benchmarks—grounding evaluation in concrete experimental results.
These papers focus on how to measure, benchmark, and compare RAG systems, including metrics, evaluation frameworks, and systematic empirical comparisons.

children.title: Specialized RAG Extensions: Personalization, Domain Adaptation, and Alternative Paradigms
children.rationale: These papers extend RAG beyond the standard paradigm toward user-centric personalization, domain-specific knowledge graphs, enhanced agent architectures, and alternative augmentation strategies such as cache-augmented generation.

rationale: The RAG literature naturally partitions into four progressive layers: foundational concepts and surveys, core technical methods (retrieval, fusion, generation), evaluation and benchmarking, and specialized applications/extensions.
